state.task: Two agents analysed Java code for path traversal (CWE-22). Their final answers follow, then the code of each method in question.
agent_answers: {"findings": [{"cwe": "CWE-22", "class": "Unpacker", "method": "process", "explanation": "The ZipUtil.Unpacker.process method directly uses attacker-controlled zip entry names from ZipEntry.getName() as file paths without any validation or sanitization. The entry name is passed through the mapper.map() function but this does not prevent path traversal attacks. When the entry name is used to construct a File object with new File(outputDir, name), it can create files outside the intended output directory, allowing an attacker to write files to arbitrary locations on the filesystem. This occurs because the zip entry name is treated as a direct path component without proper containment checks or path normalization."}]}

{"findings": [{"cwe": "CWE-22", "class": "Unpacker", "method": "process", "explanation": "In Unpacker.process, the ZIP entry name from zipEntry.getName() is mapped and used directly in new File(outputDir, name) without any containment check or path normalization; FileUtils.copy(in, file) then writes to that attacker-controlled path, allowing directory traversal."}]}
